page_title: TuckBar · Hide the macOS menu bar, per monitor

summary.name: TuckBar
summary.one_liner: TuckBar is a macOS app that hides the menu bar on selected displays (per monitor), such as an OLED, while leaving it visible on other screens.
keywords: hide menu bar on one display
hide menu bar when plugging in monitor
use_cases: Hide the static menu bar on an OLED to reduce burn-in risk
Keep a clean wallpaper on one monitor while keeping the menu bar on others
Temporarily show the menu bar while screen recording
Auto-hide the menu bar and Dock when a specific display is connected
summary.what_it_does: TuckBar lets you tag specific displays and hide the macOS menu bar on them while keeping it on the rest. It works by reading the real wallpaper pixels behind the bar and painting them over the strip, so the bar appears to disappear rather than turning black. Moving the cursor to the top edge reveals the real bar, and moving away tucks it again. You can untuck for 5 to 60 minutes, and it re-tucks automatically when the timer ends. It can also tuck when a tagged display is connected, optionally hide the Dock, and restore the bar on quit or after a force-quit on next launch.
notable: Per-monitor menu bar hiding, which the page says no macOS API provides
Wallpaper pixels are read live and painted over the bar, so it looks seamless
Timed untuck from 5 to 60 minutes, then re-tucks automatically
Optional Dock hiding tied to tagged display connection
caveats: Pricing and licensing are not stated on the page
Overlay approach means the bar is covered rather than removed, and the page does not describe other limitations
